h1:
Koh Kood for Couples
Quiet Beaches, Seaside Dinners & Sunsets
intro: Koh Kood is the southernmost island in Trat, and it's still quieter with clearer water than a lot of the big-name islands. For a couples' trip, the real draw here is the quiet — beaches where no one walks past all day, seafood dinners on a wooden deck over the water, and west-coast sunsets you can catch almost every evening. We've put together a relaxed 3-day, 2-night plan with no rushing, just slow time together.

blocks.html: If you want a beach trip where you're not fighting anyone for a photo spot, Koh Kood suits couples better than the busier islands. It's a big island with few people, and several beaches have a single resort running the whole bay, so you can walk the entire stretch with just the two of you. This plan is built around sleeping in, eating fresh seafood, catching the sunset every evening, and leaving slack in the day so you don't wear yourselves out.

blocks.text: Before you go: a few things so there are no surprises

blocks.html: Koh Kood is a long trip and the timing takes some planning. Driving from Bangkok to Laem Sok pier in Trat takes about 5–6 hours, then it's another 1–1.5 hours by ferry or speedboat. Boonsiri runs several departures a day in high season, but book your boat ahead, especially on weekends and long holidays.

items: Season — The good window is Nov–Apr: clear sea, small waves. During the monsoon (May–Oct) the rain is heavy and many resorts and boats shut down, so always check before booking.
Prices on the island run higher than the mainland — Water, food, fuel, everything comes over by boat. Resort restaurant dishes commonly run into the hundreds of THB each, so budget a little extra.

Signal and power — Some beaches have weak or no mobile signal, and some resorts only run power at set hours. It's part of the charm of switching off, but if you need to work, check with your accommodation first.

Getting around the island — The roads are narrow with steep climbs and descents, and some stretches are dirt. If you rent a motorbike, ride carefully, especially at night when there's almost no street lighting.

blocks.title: Time your boat right
blocks.html: If you leave Bangkok very early, you'll catch an afternoon boat and reach your room just before the first sunset. But if you leave late, it's worth staying one night on the Trat side and taking a morning boat — that way you're not rushing and you won't miss the last departure.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Arrive, settle in, then catch your first sunset

items.activity: Leave Bangkok and head for Laem Sok pier in Trat
items.note: About 5–6 hrs if you drive yourself, or take a van/coach to Trat and connect with the boat company's shuttle

items.activity: Take the boat across to Koh Kood, about 1–1.5 hrs from Laem Sok
items.note: Book your departure ahead · large bags go in the hold below, keep valuables with you

items.activity: Check in, unpack, rest after the journey
items.note: If you're staying on a west-coast beach like Ao Phrao or Ao Ngamkho, you can watch the sunset right from your room

items.activity: Stroll the beach in front of your room, drink in hand, waiting for the evening light
items.note: The west-coast beaches are quiet this evening — good for couple photos with no one walking through

items.activity: Watch the first sunset from the beach or the resort's wooden pier
items.note: Ao Phrao and Ao Ngamkho face west, so you see the sun drop straight into the sea

items.activity: First dinner at the resort's beachside restaurant
items.note: You're tired from travelling the first night, so eating close to your room is easier — no driving in the dark

blocks.html: Don't cram the first evening with activities. Let your body adjust after the long trip. Just sitting down to eat, listening to the waves with the person next to you, is already worth the trip.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Quiet beaches, a waterfall, then a seafood dinner at Ao Salat

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: A full day with no rush

items.activity: Easy breakfast at your accommodation, no need to hurry
items.note: Today is all about relaxed sightseeing — save your energy for the sunset this evening

items.activity: Visit Khlong Chao Waterfall and swim in the freshwater pool
items.note: The island's main waterfall, a short walk in · there's more water and it's prettier after rain

items.activity: Stop by Khlong Chao Beach — fine sand and shallow water, good for a walk and photos
items.note: A mid-island beach with a laid-back feel and a waterside café nearby

items.activity: Lunch at a waterside café in the Khlong Chao area
items.note: There are several stilted wooden cafés over the water — sit with a coffee and the canal view for as long as you like

items.activity: Head to a quiet southern beach, like Ao Phrao or a quiet white-sand beach near your room
items.note: Ao Phrao is a long white-sand beach with shallow water and few people — good for lazing about, just the two of you

items.activity: Drive or ride to the Ao Salat fishing village on the east coast
items.note: Narrow roads with hills — drive slowly and carefully · get there before dusk so you can walk the fish pier

items.activity: Seafood dinner at a village spot in Ao Salat, picking fresh seafood from the pens
items.note: Places like Red, Jack, and Captain Nong are local waterside spots — fresh seafood at seasonal prices

items.activity: Head back, sit on the balcony and end the day to the sound of the sea
items.note: The roads are dark at night — keep your lights on, drive slowly, and watch for animals crossing

blocks.title: Want dinner with the sunset
blocks.html: To line dinner up with the evening light, pick a restaurant or café on the west coast (around Ao Phrao–Khlong Chao) and book a waterside table for 17:30–18:00 · Ao Salat is on the east coast, so it's stronger on fresh seafood and the fishing-village feel than on sunsets.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Catch the last moments before the boat

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: An easy morning, then the trip home

items.activity: Breakfast, pack up, double-check your return boat time
items.note: Checkout is usually around 11:00–12:00 — ask your accommodation about a pier shuttle ahead of time

items.activity: One last couple walk and photos on the beach in front of your room
items.note: The morning light is soft and the water clear — good for photos to remember the trip before you leave

items.activity: Stop at a photo spot along the way, like the giant Makha tree or a roadside viewpoint
items.note: Pick a spot on the way to the pier so you don't have to double back

items.activity: Take the boat back to Laem Sok pier, then continue your journey
items.note: Allow at least 30 minutes to reach the pier before your departure — more if you've got a lot of luggage

blocks.html: Don't force a packed last day. Keep it light, because the way back still means hours on a boat and then in a car. Save your energy for the journey and it'll be a smoother trip home.

items.name: Ao Phrao
items.blurb: A long white-sand beach on the southwest coast with shallow water, gentle waves, and few people. It faces straight into the sunset, so it's perfect for sitting out and waiting for the evening light, just the two of you.

items.name: Secret Sunset Beach
items.blurb: A small beach near Ao Phrao with no signs — you have to walk down a little dirt path. You see the sun drop into the sea with nothing in the way. Go before evening and it's easier to find a spot.

items.name: West-coast resort piers and wooden jetties
items.blurb: Many west-coast resorts have wooden jetties reaching out over the water — a lovely place to take couple photos at sunset without going far.

blocks.text: How to pick the right place to stay as a couple

items: Want to watch the sunset from bed — Choose a west-coast place around Ao Phrao, Ao Ngamkho, or a white-sand beach.
Want easy access to food and cafés — The Khlong Chao area is mid-island and has more restaurants and cafés to choose from than the other beaches.
Want the quietest, most cut-off spot — A beach with a single resort running the whole bay is very quiet and private, but you trade away having fewer restaurant choices.
Always check before booking — Resorts open by season and many close during the monsoon. Ask about power, water, signal, and the pier shuttle before you send a deposit.

faq.q: How many days do you need for a couples' trip to Koh Kood?
faq.a: 3 days and 2 nights is about right, because Koh Kood is a long trip. With just 2 days and 1 night you'll spend more time on the car-and-boat journey than actually exploring · if you have 4 days, even better — you can leave a day to do nothing at all without rushing.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Koh Kood?
faq.a: Nov–Apr is the best window: clear sea, small waves, good weather · May–Oct is the monsoon season with heavy rain when many boats and resorts close, so always check before you plan.

faq.q: Where's the best place to watch the sunset on Koh Kood?
faq.a: The west-coast beaches and resorts get a good sunset almost every evening. The spots couples like are Ao Phrao, the secret beach near Ao Phrao, and the wooden jetties of the west-coast seaside resorts.

faq.q: Where do you go for a seafood dinner on Koh Kood?
faq.a: The Ao Salat fishing village on the east coast has seafood spots where you pick fresh catch straight from the pens, like Red, Jack, and Captain Nong · resorts and beachside cafés around the island also have seafood menus, at prices that depend on the season and what's available that day.

faq.q: How do you get around Koh Kood?
faq.a: Most people rent a motorbike or use the resort shuttle · the island roads are narrow with steep climbs and descents, some stretches are dirt, and there's little street lighting at night, so take extra care if you drive yourself, especially after rain when the roads are slippery.
